advances: A classification of finite weighted base eligibility and its support sources, without a mixed cap-depth bound at a nonvertex.

proof:
The feasible mass is the value of the finite linear program maximizing $\sum_z m_z$ under $0\le m_z\le w_z$ and $\sum_z m_z(z-j)=0$: every submeasure gives these masses and constant density $m_z/w_z$ realizes each allocation. The program is feasible and compact. Introducing a free multiplier $a$ for base balance and eliminating the upper-bound multipliers gives the dual
$$
T(j)=\min_{a\in\mathbb R^n}\sum_{z\in P}w_z(1+a\cdot(z-j))_+.
$$
Finite linear-programming duality and attainment apply, since the primal is feasible and bounded and the dual is feasible at $a=0$. At a vertex a base functional strictly exposes $j$ among the other sites, so balanced mass uses only its fiber and the isolating closed cap and the inevitable own mass give $T(j)=D(j)=w_j$. For a singleton base the same statements hold directly.

For a minimizing $a$ write $q_z=1+a\cdot(z-j)$. Every level $\{q_z\ge s\}$ for $0<s\le1$ is the trace of a containing closed halfspace, or the whole base set if $a=0$, so its mass is at least $D(j)$. Integrating over $s>0$ gives the dual objective and proves the inequality. Equality excludes $q_z>1$ by its positive contribution above level one, and excludes $0<q_z<1$ because it makes the level mass drop across an interior threshold while the level mass must equal $D(j)$ almost everywhere on $(0,1)$. Thus every positive $q_z$ equals one. Put $F=\{z:q_z=1\}$; the dual value is $\sum_{z\in F}w_z$. If $z_0\ne j$ is another point of $F$, choose $b$ with $b\cdot(z_0-j)<0$. For sufficiently large $A$, the functional $Aa+b$ is negative on $z_0-j$ and on all $z-j$ for $z\notin F$, since the latter have $a\cdot(z-j)<0$. It is nonzero and the closed cap through $j$ with this functional then has mass strictly less than $T(j)$, a contradiction. Hence $F=\{j\}$, so $j$ is a vertex.

For the moment conclusions write $Q_s(j)$ for the set of raw continuous moments at feasible mass $s$ and base mean $j$, so that $M_t(j)=Q_t(j)/t$. Masses $0$ and $T(j)$ are feasible and every intermediate mass is obtained by scaling. The compact graph and strict ball inclusion in 8c6a53dd27e5c125 apply with feasible constraint pairs $(0,0)$ and $(T(j),T(j)j)$, which are distinct because $T(j)\ge w_j>0$. Thus $Q_t(j)$ is full-dimensional for $0<t<T(j)$. Fix any $u\ne0$. The function $s\mapsto h_{Q_s(j)}(u)$ is finite and concave on $[0,T(j)]$ by convexity of the joint graph. At an interior $t$ it has a finite supporting slope $b$. With $q_0$ an attained support point at $t$, the plane $u\cdot q\le u\cdot q_0+b(s-t)$ supports the same joint graph. Apply c9b7d48527d3d6a1 at this $t,j,u,b$ to obtain a cap $\{u\cdot x+a\cdot(z-j)-b\ge0\}$ of mass $t$ and base mean $j$ realizing $q_0$, with finite $a$. The support density is unique by 8c6a53dd27e5c125 on the same fixed constraint pair (or directly since a nonzero continuous cap normal has null level on every positive fiber). Division by $t$ leaves the support direction and the representing density unchanged. At a vertex all balanced densities are confined to its one fiber. At mass $w_j$ the density must be one there, so its continuous centroid is the singleton asserted. Lower positive masses give the full-dimensional one-fiber trimmed body by the same interpolation. At a nonvertex strictness $t\le D(j)<T(j)$ gives the claimed full-dimensionality and cap attainment.

statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, let $\mu$ be the summed $d$-volume of the positive sampled fibers $K_z$ of a compact convex body, and let their finite nonempty base set be $P$ with weights $w_z=|K_z|$. At $j\in P$ let $D(j)$ be the infimum of $\sum_{z\in H}w_z$ over closed base halfspaces containing $j$, and let $T(j)$ be the maximum mass of a submeasure of $\mu$ with base mean $j$. Then $T(j)\ge D(j)$, with equality exactly when $j$ is a vertex of $\operatorname{conv}P$, and in that case both equal $w_j$.

For $0<t\le D(j)$ let $M_t(j)$ be the continuous centroid body of submeasures of mass $t$ and base mean $j$. If $j$ is not a vertex then $t<T(j)$, $M_t(j)$ is full-dimensional, and in every nonzero continuous direction its support is represented by a unique source density up to null sets, the indicator of an actual closed cap of mass $t$ and base mean $j$ with a finite base tilt. At a vertex the body is the ordinary one-fiber trimmed centroid body when $t<w_j$, and the singleton own-fiber centroid when $t=w_j$. These are all eligible singleton cases.
title: Exact marginal depth equality and strict feasible mass
